sentences: Venus, goddess of love, born from sea foam, drifts ashore on a scallop shell.
On the left, Zephyr, the west wind, blows her toward land; on the right, a goddess of the seasons rushes to wrap her in a flowered cloak.
At a time when most large paintings were Christian, devoting a canvas this size to a pagan nude was a bold choice.
Her pose borrows from ancient sculpture, yet her neck is impossibly long and her left shoulder slopes strangely.
Botticelli chose flowing, graceful line over anatomical accuracy.
Look closely at her windblown hair and you will find traces of gold.
